A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Light Forcing with the same authors and core framework. All 14 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations on Self Forcing and LongLive, component ablations, retrieval sensitivity experiments, qualitative comparisons, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds 15-second generation evaluations, additional acceleration baselines, qualitative ablations, and hardware and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises HSA's stated procedure to always include sink and nearby frames and select blocks jointly across selected frames, replacing v1's per-frame top-k specification. These are localized refinements to the retained framework. Dense attention for the first chunk was already specified in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates 5-second generation on VBench. v2 adds 15-second generation on VBench-Long using Infinite-Forcing, introducing substantially longer autoregressive rollouts and their temporal-consistency demands while retaining the original coverage.

E2.justification: The original Self Forcing and LongLive comparator sets remain unchanged. v2 Appendix G and Table 8 add evaluated comparisons with TeaCache and DyCoke, substantially broadening comparison scope beyond sparse attention to feature caching and token reduction.

E3.justification: The stated 5-second target sparsity changes from 0.90 to 0.88; v2 additionally specifies a 15-second configuration with target/base sparsity 0.85/0.95. New experiments introduce baseline adaptation settings, GPU-specific deployment configurations, and peak-memory evaluation. The changed short-video setting does not establish that the retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: The original quantitative component and retrieval-sensitivity ablations are retained. v2 Appendix F adds controlled long-video comparisons of fixed sparsity, CAG, and CAG plus HSA, examining noise, color degradation, and white-band artifacts. Appendix H adds staged deployment and memory analyses across hardware and durations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed summaries, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's description of timing one video after warm-up concerns measurement procedure rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All retained benchmark and quantitative ablation entries match. New results include 15-second Total Scores of 84.1 for Light Forcing versus 83.6 for dense attention, TeaCache/DyCoke comparisons, and hardware and memory measurements. Optimized deployment changes from 19.7 FPS and 2.33x speedup to 27.4 FPS and 3.08x under a revised deployment stack, not an unchanged-setting comparison.

T1.justification: Equation (6) corrects the allocation constraint to exclude the dense first chunk, while Equations (7)–(11) revise candidate-set definitions and formalize joint frame–block selection. The Markov-chain, KL, and Pinsker derivation is retained from v1 Appendix B in v2 Appendix C; its notation corrections do not constitute a new proof.

C1.justification: The novelty claim, two central contributions, and 84.5 VBench claim remain. The abstract and introduction broaden the deployment contribution from 2.3x acceleration on RTX 5090 to approximately 2–3x across diverse GPUs, with updated throughput claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of long-video artifacts, caching/token-reduction failures, hardware-dependent acceleration, and why sparse attention reduces latency without reducing measured peak memory. The limitations replace the unresolved Hopper-adaptation concern with A100 tuning caveats and newly acknowledge residual artifacts; the restriction to 1.3B models remains.

D1.justification: v2 changes reported code status from forthcoming to released and supplies checkpoint links, a Docker image identifier, duration-specific configurations, HSA activation conditions, qualitative prompts, baseline adaptation details, and device-specific kernel information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although v1 Appendix A's explicit selected-block-count formula is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds related-work citations such as Mixture of Contexts and Pack and Force Your Memory, references supporting the new evaluations and deployment, and discussion positioning sparse attention against caching and token reduction. It removes the Brooks world-simulator reference. The main taxonomy and novelty positioning remain; publication updates are not new works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain. Targeted rewrites clarify CAG/HSA and deployment, a Longer Generation subsection and additional appendix sections are inserted, and limitations move to Appendix J. Publication-header, correspondence, and method-label edits are limited rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds long-video examples and two qualitative ablation figures, plus tables for long-video scores, configurations, new baselines, device efficiency, and memory. The deployment chart is redrawn with an additional kernel-optimization stage. Existing benchmark displays are retained, and v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 10 rather than a new result.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited support for long-rollout and deployment claims through 15-second evaluation, controlled qualitative ablations, comparisons beyond sparse attention, and hardware and memory analyses. Configuration and release information also improve reproducibility. The retained scores are not clearly reconciled with the revised short-video sparsity setting, but this remaining ambiguity does not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and explicit applicability limits.
